question: Give an example of going above and beyond what was expected of you.

raiseTranscript.text: My task was to implement a small feature in the backend service. After finishing the core work, I noticed the logging was inconsistent and would make debugging hard later, so I added structured logs and wrote a short internal doc on how to use them.
What prompted you to do that?
The team was onboarding two new engineers that month and I remembered how long it took me to trace issues when I joined.

raiseNotes: Q: Give an example of going above and beyond what was expected of you.
Junior backend dev, individual task on feature
Added structured logging + doc after core work done
Outcome: new hires ramped faster on debugging
Quote: "I remembered how long it took me to trace issues when I joined"
Follow-up: Asked why they chose logging; said it was from own onboarding pain
junior.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar on Initiative for a junior. The candidate took an individual task and extended it with a small but useful improvement based on their recent experience. Quote: "I remembered how long it took me to trace issues when I joined." This shows ownership of their own work and basic coachability from past feedback. The impact stayed local but was concrete. Biggest strength is the direct link between personal learning and proactive action without being asked.

lowerTranscript.text: I finished my assigned tickets early so I stayed late a few nights to help the support team with tickets even though that wasn't my job.
Did your manager know or was this coordinated?
Not really, I just wanted to show I care about the team.

lowerNotes: Q: Give an example of going above and beyond what was expected of you.
Junior stayed late to help support without coordination
No metrics or outcome mentioned
Quote: "I just wanted to show I care about the team"
Follow-up: Manager awareness? Candidate said no coordination
junior.lowerFeedback: Lowers the bar for a junior on Initiative. The story shows extra hours but no ownership of results or learning from feedback. Quote: "I just wanted to show I care about the team." Effort was uncoordinated and produced no visible improvement in support or their own skills. The gap is lack of scope awareness and failure to connect actions to outcomes.

raiseTranscript.text: I was leading a migration for my service. Two other teams had similar work coming up so I wrote a shared runbook and ran two brown-bag sessions. Three teams used it and cut their migration time by about 30%.
How did you get the other teams to adopt it?
I asked their tech leads for input on the first draft and made changes based on their constraints.

raiseNotes: Q: Give an example of going above and beyond what was expected of you.
Senior led service migration, created shared runbook
Ran brown bags, influenced two other teams without authority
Outcome: 30% time reduction across teams
Quote: "I asked their tech leads for input on the first draft"
Follow-up: Adoption method; said sought input from leads first
senior.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar at senior level. The candidate moved beyond their own service to create cross-team leverage with a runbook and sessions. Quote: "I asked their tech leads for input on the first draft." Shows influence without authority and measurable impact. Story includes clear metrics and evidence of raising the bar for peers. Biggest strength is the proactive identification of duplication before it became a problem.

lowerTranscript.text: My project was behind so I worked weekends to finish the code myself instead of waiting on the design team.
Did this change how the team worked going forward?
Not really, it was just that one deadline.

lowerNotes: Q: Give an example of going above and beyond what was expected of you.
Senior worked weekends to unblock own project
No cross-team or lasting change
Quote: "it was just that one deadline"
Follow-up: Long-term impact? None reported
senior.lowerFeedback: Lowers the bar for senior. Heroic individual effort on a deadline with no broader influence or process improvement. Quote: "it was just that one deadline." Lacks evidence of cross-team impact or raising others. The gap is treating proactivity as personal overtime rather than systemic leverage.

raiseTranscript.text: Our on-call load was burning out the team. I created a rotation with two other teams, negotiated the handoff process, and trained two engineers to run the new process. On-call pages dropped 40% and we promoted one of the trained engineers.
How did you handle resistance from the other managers?
I showed them the ticket volume data first and let them propose the rotation split.

raiseNotes: Q: Give an example of going above and beyond what was expected of you.
Manager addressed team on-call burnout
Created cross-team rotation, trained others, negotiated with peers
Outcome: 40% page reduction + one promotion
Quote: "I showed them the ticket volume data first"
Follow-up: Handling resistance; used data and let peers propose split
manager.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar at manager level. The candidate owned a team health problem and created leverage through cross-team process and development of others. Quote: "I showed them the ticket volume data first." Demonstrates handling underperformance signals early and producing team-level outcomes. Biggest strength is the combination of data-driven influence and deliberate people development.

lowerTranscript.text: The team was missing deadlines so I started reviewing every PR myself to keep quality up.
What happened to the team's ownership after that?
They got faster at shipping but still waited for my review.

lowerNotes: Q: Give an example of going above and beyond what was expected of you.
Manager reviewed all PRs to fix quality
No delegation or process change
Quote: "They got faster at shipping but still waited for my review"
Follow-up: Long-term team ownership? Remained dependent
manager.lowerFeedback: Lowers the bar for manager. Extra work created dependency instead of leverage. Quote: "They got faster at shipping but still waited for my review." Shows no development of the team or sustainable process. The gap is substituting personal effort for building team capability.

raiseTranscript.text: Revenue in one region was flat for two years. I sponsored a small team to test a new go-to-market motion outside our core product. After the pilot we rolled it to three regions and it became 18% of that year's incremental revenue.
What made you start the pilot when the core business was stable?
The data showed our addressable market in that region was shrinking; waiting would have made the problem bigger in 18 months.

raiseNotes: Q: Give an example of going above and beyond what was expected of you.
Exec spotted regional stagnation risk
Sponsored out-of-core pilot, scaled to three regions
Outcome: 18% of incremental revenue
Quote: "The data showed our addressable market in that region was shrinking"
Follow-up: Why act on stable numbers; cited 18-month forward risk
exec.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar at exec level. The candidate exercised strategic judgment on long-term market risk and created new revenue leverage. Quote: "The data showed our addressable market in that region was shrinking." Shows high ambiguity tolerance and org-level impact without heroics. Biggest strength is the forward-looking trade-off that protected the business.

lowerTranscript.text: I personally negotiated a key renewal that was at risk and closed it in two weeks.
Did this change how the organization handles renewals?
We documented the case but the process stayed the same.

lowerNotes: Q: Give an example of going above and beyond what was expected of you.
Exec stepped in on one renewal
No org process change
Quote: "We documented the case but the process stayed the same"
Follow-up: Systemic impact? None beyond documentation
exec.lowerFeedback: Lowers the bar at exec level. Individual rescue on a single deal with no lasting organizational leverage. Quote: "We documented the case but the process stayed the same." Shows tactical action instead of strategic judgment or building scalable mechanisms. The gap is absence of long-term thinking or trade-off decisions.

diagnostic.manager: Used data to align other managers

diagnostic.exec: Created new motion others could run
